A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MobileOcc and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete supplementary Sections A–D. Renumbered and merged material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original human-mesh evaluations, MobileOcc occupancy and velocity benchmarks, and supplementary component ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds occupancy-label validation and manual detection-quality audits.

M1.justification: The CLIFF initialization, visibility filtering, ICP alignment, SMPL optimization losses, static mapping, and occupancy fusion remain unchanged. The velocity-head adaptation also already appears in v1. Additional voxelization explanations do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use CODa/MobileOcc, 3DPW, SLOPER4D, and HumanM3 with the same underlying perception tasks. The new annotation audits examine retained data and existing crowd/lighting conditions; they do not introduce another dataset, domain, or distinct input scenario. OpenScene appears only in a descriptive comparison.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the human-mesh and MobileOcc benchmarks. Merging the real-LiDAR tables retains their methods, including CLIFF. The new dataset-comparison table does not constitute an experimental baseline addition.

E3.justification: New Section 4.2 introduces label validation on four CODa sequences containing 400 frames and a separate 300-frame detection audit. Protocols include bounding-box references excluding the bottom 0.1 m, camera-frustum-restricted LiDAR body references, and a one-voxel matching tolerance at 0.2 m resolution. Existing benchmark splits, training settings, and evaluation grids remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial analyses of static-label accuracy, pedestrian-label agreement against two proxy references, and upstream detection reliability across crowd density and nighttime conditions. These directly investigate annotation reliability and failure conditions. The supplementary visibility-filter and loss-term ablations are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: The supplementary means, standard deviations, t-values, and p-values retain the same reporting practices and values. The new audits report counts and aggregate metrics without adding repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or significance procedures.

E6.justification: New Tables 4–5 report static-label mIoU of 71.2, pedestrian F1 of 83.1 against bounding boxes and 92.5 against LiDAR body references, and nighttime detection recall of 76.9%. Separately, Panoptic-FlashOcc's PQ-dagger/RQ/SQ values change from 28.1/65.8/32.6 in v1 Table 5 to 32.6/28.1/65.8 in v2 Table 7. These are revised metric assignments, not established performance gains; other matched benchmark and appendix results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The optimization objective, component losses, and supplementary visibility-filter definitions in Equations 1–10 are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: a human-aware occupancy dataset, an RGB–LiDAR annotation pipeline, and occupancy/velocity benchmarks. The additional validation supports these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of taxonomy mismatch, bounding-box overcoverage, LiDAR-surface matching, nighttime misses, and error propagation into static maps. It also explains why interpenetration should minimally affect occupancy and newly acknowledges that SMPL excludes carried or accompanying objects. The new text inconsistently describes voxelization as surface-based in Section 3.2.3 and volume-filling in Section 4.2.3.

D1.justification: The abstract newly states that code and data are released and supplies a project-page link. v2 also documents daytime/nighttime sequence distinctions and reference-construction details for the new audits. Existing supplementary hyperparameters, hardware, optimization, preprocessing, and training information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Table 1 explicitly compares human modeling and instance tracking across datasets, adds OpenScene, and sharpens MobileOcc's novelty positioning. The condensed related work removes the FB-OCC, PIFu, and ICON references, while retaining the principal research framing.

P1.justification: The main text undergoes broad condensation and rewriting across related work, preprocessing, CLIFF initialization, metric explanations, and benchmark details. Benchmark material moves from Section 4.2 into a standalone Section 5 with a revised subsection hierarchy. Introductory motivation is expanded, while the appendices remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds the dataset-comparison table and two validation tables, merges v1 Tables 2–3 into Table 3 and Tables 5–6 into Table 7, and redesigns the occupancy table using color-coded class headers and a separate legend. Main-table captions and placement are revised. Figures 1–5 and supplementary displays are retained.

improvement.justification: Section 4.2 adds useful direct checks of dataset labels and exposes nighttime detection failures that v1 did not quantify. Access information and the carried-object limitation also improve usability and transparency. These benefits are limited by proxy-based pedestrian references, the one-voxel tolerance, and inconsistent surface-versus-volume voxelization descriptions; the new evidence strengthens confidence without fully resolving annotation-validity questions.
